{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | image = [[File:総社神社 (坂出市) 正面鳥居.JPG|250px|]]
Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | image = [[File:総社神社 (坂出市) 正面鳥居.JPG|250px|]]
Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | image = [[File:総社神社 (坂出市) 正面鳥居.JPG|250px|]]
Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | image = [[File:総社神社 (坂出市) 正面鳥居.JPG|250px|]]
Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | image = [[File:総社神社 (坂出市) 正面鳥居.JPG|250px|]]
Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | image = [[File:総社神社 (坂出市) 正面鳥居.JPG|250px|]]
Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | image = [[File:総社神社 (坂出市) 正面鳥居.JPG|250px|]]
Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach.
