[[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | image = [[File:総社神社 (坂出市) 正面鳥居.JPG|250px|]]
Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]

[[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]
[[Izanami]]
All local deities of Sanuki Province | shrine_rank = [[Sanuki Province]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) main hall.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: tier 5]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja Shrine (Sakide)]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kagawa Prefecture]] [[Category:Sakaide, Kagawa]] [[Category:Gō-sha]] [[Category:Sanuki Province]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Q11]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Sōja Shrine (Sakide)]] [[sn:ōja Shrine (Sakide)]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Sōja Shrine Sakaide}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Sōja Shrine (Sakide)}}

[[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. 正面鳥居 |所在地 = [[香川県]][[坂出市]]林田町惣社3001 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=総社神社}} |祭神 = [[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]]
[[イザナミ|伊弉冉尊]]
国中大小神祇 |神体 = |社格 = [[讃岐国]][[総社]]
旧[[郷社]] |創建 = （伝）[[延長 (元号)|延長]]4年（[[926年]]） |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = |神事 = }} '''総社神社'''（そうじゃじんじゃ）は、[[香川県]][[坂出市]]にある[[神社]]。[[讃岐国]][[総社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[郷社]]。 == 概要 == [[古代]]、[[国司]]は各国内の全ての神社を[[一宮]]から順に巡拝していた。これを効率化するため、各国の[[国府]]近くに国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]を設け、まとめて祭祀を行うようになった。総社神社はそのうちの[[讃岐国]]の総社にあたる。 当社は[[坂出市]]東部の平地に位置し、讃岐国府からは北方約5.5kmの距離にある。社記の『讃岐国名勝図会』には「惣社大明神は阿野北郡林田郷松ヶ浦今は総社といふに鎮座す。御社、今は海汀とは五、六丁もへだたれど、今も御社の近きわたり深く掘りみれば貝のからなどいと多かるとて、昔は海辺なる事しるべし」と記されている『香川県の地名』総社神社項。。 == 祭神 == * [[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]] （いざなぎのみこと） * [[イザナミ|伊弉冉尊]] （いざなみのみこと） * 国中大小神祇 - 讃岐国内の神々。 == 歴史 == 社伝では[[延長 (元号)|延長]]4年（[[926年]]）の創建とする。創建後は讃岐国府の総社として毎年国司の奉幣を受けたという。 [[嘉慶 (日本)|嘉慶]]年間（[[1387年]]-[[1389年]]）の兵火で社殿は焼失し、[[細川頼之]]により[[明徳]]元年（[[1390年]]）に再建された。その後衰退していたのを[[天文 (元号)|天文]]20年（[[1551年]]）に[[三好氏]]一族によって再興されたが、[[天正]]年間（[[1573年]]-[[1592年]]）に兵火で再び焼失した。そして、[[慶長]]2年（[[1597年]]）に新しく社殿が建てられたという。 == 境内 == 一の鳥居は[[香川県道186号大屋冨築港宇多津線|県道186号線]]を渡り神社正面から伸びる道を進んだ突き当りに位置する。鳥居をくぐり右手には[[御旅所]]がある。 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 本殿.JPG|本殿 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|拝殿 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|一の鳥居 == 摂末社 == 厳島神社ほか数社が境内に鎮座する。 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|厳島神社 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|境内社 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[香川県]][[坂出市]]林田町惣社3001 '''交通アクセス''' * [[坂出駅]]（[[四国旅客鉄道|JR四国]][[予讃線]]）から、[[琴参バス]]で「総社神社前」バス停下車 '''周辺''' * 讃岐国府跡（{{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=讃岐国府跡}}） - 南方約5.5km。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内掲示板 * 『日本歴史地名体系 香川県の地名』（[[平凡社]]）坂出市 総社神社項 {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:そうしやしんしやさかいてし}} [[Category:香川県の神社]] [[Category:坂出市の歴史]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:香川県の旧郷社]] [[Category:讃岐国|社0]] [[Category:坂出市の建築物]]

旧[[郷社]] |創建 = （伝）[[延長 (元号)|延長]]4年（[[926年]]） |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = |神事 = }} '''総社神社'''（そうじゃじんじゃ）は、[[香川県]][[坂出市]]にある[[神社]]。[[讃岐国]][[総社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[郷社]]。 == 概要 == [[古代]]、[[国司]]は各国内の全ての神社を[[一宮]]から順に巡拝していた。これを効率化するため、各国の[[国府]]近くに国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]を設け、まとめて祭祀を行うようになった。総社神社はそのうちの[[讃岐国]]の総社にあたる。 当社は[[坂出市]]東部の平地に位置し、讃岐国府からは北方約5.5kmの距離にある。社記の『讃岐国名勝図会』には「惣社大明神は阿野北郡林田郷松ヶ浦今は総社といふに鎮座す。御社、今は海汀とは五、六丁もへだたれど、今も御社の近きわたり深く掘りみれば貝のからなどいと多かるとて、昔は海辺なる事しるべし」と記されている『香川県の地名』総社神社項。。 == 祭神 == * [[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]] （いざなぎのみこと） * [[イザナミ|伊弉冉尊]] （いざなみのみこと） * 国中大小神祇 - 讃岐国内の神々。 == 歴史 == 社伝では[[延長 (元号)|延長]]4年（[[926年]]）の創建とする。創建後は讃岐国府の総社として毎年国司の奉幣を受けたという。 [[嘉慶 (日本)|嘉慶]]年間（[[1387年]]-[[1389年]]）の兵火で社殿は焼失し、[[細川頼之]]により[[明徳]]元年（[[1390年]]）に再建された。その後衰退していたのを[[天文 (元号)|天文]]20年（[[1551年]]）に[[三好氏]]一族によって再興されたが、[[天正]]年間（[[1573年]]-[[1592年]]）に兵火で再び焼失した。そして、[[慶長]]2年（[[1597年]]）に新しく社殿が建てられたという。 == 境内 == 一の鳥居は[[香川県道186号大屋冨築港宇多津線|県道186号線]]を渡り神社正面から伸びる道を進んだ突き当りに位置する。鳥居をくぐり右手には[[御旅所]]がある。 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 本殿.JPG|本殿 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|拝殿 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|一の鳥居 == 摂末社 == 厳島神社ほか数社が境内に鎮座する。 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|厳島神社 ファイル:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|境内社 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[香川県]][[坂出市]]林田町惣社3001 '''交通アクセス''' * [[坂出駅]]（[[四国旅客鉄道|JR四国]][[予讃線]]）から、[[琴参バス]]で「総社神社前」バス停下車 '''周辺''' * 讃岐国府跡（{{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=讃岐国府跡}}） - 南方約5.5km。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内掲示板 * 『日本歴史地名体系 香川県の地名』（[[平凡社]]）坂出市 総社神社項 {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:そうしやしんしやさかいてし}} [[Category:香川県の神社]] [[Category:坂出市の歴史]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:香川県の旧郷社]] [[Category:讃岐国|社0]] [[Category:坂出市の建築物]]

Main torii gate | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34|20|03.58|N|133|53|24.41|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Izanagi]]

Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 本殿.JPG|Main sanctuary (''honden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 拝殿.JPG|Worship hall (''haiden'') File:総社神社 (坂出市) 一の鳥居.JPG|Primary torii gate == Subordinate Shrines == Several smaller shrines, including an [[Itsukushima Shrine]] and other auxiliary shrines, are located within the grounds. File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内厳島神社.JPG|Itsukushima Shrine File:総社神社 (坂出市) 境内社.JPG|Auxiliary shrine == Access == * '''location''': 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture * By public transport: Take a [[Kotohira Bus]] from [[Sakaide Station]] ([[Yosan Line|JR Yosan Line]]) to the "Sōja Shrine Mae" stop. == Nearby Sites == * '''Sanuki Kokufu Site''' – Approximately 5.5 km to the south ({{Coord|34|17|36.97|N|133|55|06.25|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Sanuki Kokufu Site}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Sōja Shrine (Sakaide)}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kagawa Prefecture]] [[Category:Sakaide, Kagawa]] [[Category:Gō-sha]] [[Category:Sanuki Province]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Pages needing history import]][[ja:総社神社 (坂出市)]] }} [[sn:Sōja Shrine (Sakide)]] [[sn:ōja Shrine (Sakide)]] {{translated page|ja|総社神社 (坂出市)|version=84438453|comment=Imported full ja history}}

[[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Sakaide]], [[:en:Kagawa Prefecture|Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[:en:Izanami|Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[:en:Hosokawa Yoriyuki|Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sakaide|Sakaide]], [[:en:Kagawa Prefecture|Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[Sanuki Province]] during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:provincial governor|provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[:en:Izanami|Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[:en:Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[:en:Hosokawa Yoriyuki|Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[:en:Miyoshi clan|Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sakaide|Sakaide]], [[:en:Kagawa Prefecture|Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[:en:Sanuki Province|Sanuki Province]] during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:provincial governor|provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[:en:Izanami|Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[:en:Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[:en:Hosokawa Yoriyuki|Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[:en:Miyoshi clan|Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[:en:Tenshō|Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. It served as the [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[:en:Sanuki Province|Sanuki Province]] during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:provincial governor|provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[:en:Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[:en:Hosokawa Yoriyuki|Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[:en:Miyoshi clan|Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[:en:Tenshō|Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa | prefecture= {{ill|Sakaide|WD=Q855059}} }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sakaide|Sakaide]], [[:en:Kagawa Prefecture|Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[:en:Sanuki Province|Sanuki Province]] during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:provincial governor|provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[:en:Izanami|Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[:en:Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[:en:Hosokawa Yoriyuki|Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[:en:Miyoshi clan|Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[:en:Tenshō|Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa | prefecture= {{ill|Sakaide|WD=Q855059}} }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sakaide|Sakaide]], [[:en:Kagawa Prefecture|Kagawa Prefecture]]. It served as the [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for [[:en:Sanuki Province|Sanuki Province]] during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:provincial governor|provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''[[:en:Izanami|Izanami]]''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in [[:en:Meitoku|Meitoku]] 1 (1390) by [[:en:Hosokawa Yoriyuki|Hosokawa Yoriyuki]]. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the [[:en:Miyoshi clan|Miyoshi clan]], but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[:en:Tenshō|Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in [[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa | prefecture= {{ill|Sakaide|WD=Q855059}} }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sakaide|Sakaide]], {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|en|Kagawa Prefecture|WD=Q161454|lt=Kagawa Prefecture}}. It served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|WD=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province}} during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:provincial governor|provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''{{ill|Izanami|en|Izanami|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami}}''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in {{ill|Meitoku|en|Meitoku|WD=Q1145032|lt=Meitoku}} 1 (1390) by {{ill|Hosokawa Yoriyuki|en|Hosokawa Yoriyuki|WD=Q1139739|lt=Hosokawa Yoriyuki}}. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the {{ill|Miyoshi clan|en|Miyoshi clan|WD=Q2975329|lt=Miyoshi clan}}, but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[:en:Tenshō|Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}} 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. [[co:commons:Category:Soja-jinja (Sakaide)]][[ja:総社神社 (坂出市)]] [[co:commons:Category:Soja-jinja (Sakaide)]][[ja:総社神社 (坂出市)]] [[Category:sn_crud|TESTcommons:Category:Soja-jinja (Sakaide)]][[ja:総社神社 (坂出市)]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sōja Shrine | image = File:総社神社 (坂出市) 正面鳥居.JPG | location = 3001 Renda-chō, Sōja, Sakaide City, Kagawa Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|34.3343278|N|133.8901139|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Izanagi|WD=Q813858|1=Izanagi}} | shrine_Rank = {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|WD=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province|1=Sanuki Province}} {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja}}
Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa | prefecture= {{ill|Sakaide|WD=Q855059|1=Sakaide, Kagawa}} }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sakaide|Sakaide]], {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|en|Kagawa Prefecture|WD=Q161454|lt=Kagawa Prefecture|1=Kagawa Prefecture}}. It served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja}} (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|WD=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province|1=Sanuki Province}} during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}} and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:provincial governor|provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''{{ill|Izanami|en|Izanami|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami|1=Izanami}}''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in {{ill|Meitoku|en|Meitoku|WD=Q1145032|lt=Meitoku|1=Meitoku}} 1 (1390) by {{ill|Hosokawa Yoriyuki|en|Hosokawa Yoriyuki|WD=Q1139739|lt=Hosokawa Yoriyuki|1=Hosokawa Yoriyuki}}. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the {{ill|Miyoshi clan|en|Miyoshi clan|WD=Q2975329|lt=Miyoshi clan|1=Miyoshi clan}}, but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[:en:Tenshō|Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keichō|1=Keichō}} 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach. Former [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) | established = (Trad.) [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926) | map_type = Japan Kagawa | prefecture= {{ill|Sakaide|WD=Q855059|1=Sakaide, Kagawa}} }} '''Sōja Shrine''' (総社神社, ''Sōja Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sakaide|Sakaide]], {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|en|Kagawa Prefecture|WD=Q161454|lt=Kagawa Prefecture|1=Kagawa Prefecture}}. It served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja}} (shrine for enshrining all provincial deities) for {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|WD=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province|1=Sanuki Province}} during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}} and held the status of a [[Gōsha]] (village shrine) during the modern era. == Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:provincial governor|provincial governor]]s (''kokushi'') were required to visit and offer prayers at all major shrines within their jurisdiction. To simplify this process, ''Sōja'' shrines were established near provincial capitals, enshrining all local deities in one location. Sōja Shrine in Sakaide served this role for Sanuki Province. The shrine is located in the eastern plains of Sakaide City, about 5.5 km north of the Sanuki provincial capital site (''kokufu''). According to the ''Sanuki no Kuni Meishō Zue'' (讃岐国名勝図会), "The Sōja Daimyōjin was situated in the village of Matsugaura in the northern district of Hayashida, now known as Sōja. Although the shrine is now separated by about five or six blocks from the seashore, digging near the shrine reveals many shells, suggesting it was once by the sea.""Sanuki Province Shrine" in ''Kagawa no Chimei''. Heibonsha. == Enshrined Deities == * '''[[Izanagi]]''' (伊弉諾尊) * '''{{ill|Izanami|en|Izanami|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami|1=Izanami}}''' (伊弉冉尊) * Local deities of Sanuki Province (国中大小神祇) == History == According to shrine tradition, Sōja Shrine was established in [[Enchō (era)|Enchō]] 4 (926). It served as the provincial Sōja shrine for Sanuki Province, receiving annual offerings from the provincial governor. The shrine was destroyed by fire during the [[Kakei (Japan)|Kakei]] era (1387–1389) but was rebuilt in {{ill|Meitoku|en|Meitoku|WD=Q1145032|lt=Meitoku|1=Meitoku}} 1 (1390) by {{ill|Hosokawa Yoriyuki|en|Hosokawa Yoriyuki|WD=Q1139739|lt=Hosokawa Yoriyuki|1=Hosokawa Yoriyuki}}. It was revived again in [[Tenbun (era)|Tenbun]] 20 (1551) by the {{ill|Miyoshi clan|en|Miyoshi clan|WD=Q2975329|lt=Miyoshi clan|1=Miyoshi clan}}, but the shrine was once more destroyed during the [[:en:Tenshō|Tenshō]] period (1573–1592). Finally, the current buildings were constructed in {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keichō|1=Keichō}} 2 (1597). == Grounds == The main torii gate is located along [[Kagawa Prefectural Route 186]], leading to a path toward the shrine. A travel rest station (''otabisho'') is situated to the right of the approach.
